proposed_rules.trigger: A page captured under a knack.com integration URL (e.g. /integrations/bubble-knack) renders content belonging entirely to a third-party marketing domain (here, bubble.io's own homepage: 'Bubble uses cookies', bubble.io nav, bubble.io footer) rather than any Knack-authored integration page.
proposed_rules.decision: Flag as an out-of-scope capture and exclude from the knack.com EDS migration inventory; do not model bubble.io's homepage as a Knack page section/block. Alternative rejected: mapping the captured structure as if it were the real Knack integration page (rejected because the content and domain chrome are demonstrably not Knack's, so any block inventory derived from it would import a competitor's marketing copy into the migration).
proposed_rules.rationale: The capture pipeline followed a redirect or loaded the wrong URL; treating third-party content as page content would corrupt the migration inventory.

provenance.evidence: C90 root contains 'Bubble uses cookies', bubble.io nav/footer, no Knack branding anywhere in the tree

proposed_rules.trigger: Two nodes with near-identical text and overlapping/duplicated bounding boxes (rc7/rc8, both 'Blown away by Bubble's AI assi...') appear promoted outside their DOM parent at nearly the same position.
proposed_rules.decision: Treat as clones of a single infinite-scroll/looping carousel, not as two distinct testimonials; collapse to one testimonial-carousel block instance.
proposed_rules.rationale: Carousel libraries often duplicate slide DOM nodes for seamless looping; counting both as unique content would double the row count.

provenance.evidence: C90 rc7 @-92,8872 and rc8 @1208,8872, both 1300x722 with identical leading text

notes: This capture appears to be an off-domain page (bubble.io's own marketing homepage, not a Knack-authored integration page) — flagged as a pipeline capture-scope issue.
